question: Assume the JTB definition of Knowledge, which suggests that "Knowledge is a Justified True Belief". If our only available epistemic states are Knowledge and Belief, what are the two problems JTB runs into? Ignore Gettier problems.

1.text:
Under the tripartite analysis

K p := B p & J p & T p

and with only the two doxastic labels Knowledge and Belief left in the
language, 

B p  :=  ¬K p

Hence everything that is not justified-true-belief is lumped together as
mere Belief. The Truth × Justification space is four cells

          J        ¬J
T     K p   B p & T p & ¬J p
F     B p & J p & ¬T p   B p & ¬J p & ¬T p

K p is identified with the J & T cell. The remaining three cells are all
identified with one and the same state 'mere belief'.

In particular the analysis can no longer track justification and truth
independently of one another.

* Justified false belief. B p & J p & ¬T p is not knowledge. On the
two-state taxonomy it is mere Belief, and therefore counted as
epistemically on a par with B p & ¬J p & ¬T p, a completely unjustified
false belief, and with B p & T p & ¬J p, a true belief arrived at by
accident. A belief that is epistemically good in the respect of
justification is indistinguishable from a belief that is epistemically
bad in both respects.

* True but unjustified belief / accidental true belief. B p & T p & ¬J p
is not knowledge. On the two-state taxonomy it is also mere Belief, and
therefore counted as epistemically on a par with B p & J p & ¬T p, a
justified false belief. Truth is thereby not tracked independently of
justification: a true belief that is good in the respect of truth and
bad in the respect of justification is given the same epistemic status
as a false belief that is good in the respect of justification and bad in
the respect of truth. The space of epistemic merit collapses into
Knowledge = J & T and Belief = ¬J & T ∨ J & ¬T ∨ ¬J & ¬T.

That is the familiar collapse of the JTB space. Once you allow only
Knowledge and Belief as labels you cannot register justified false belief
as a distinct epistemically good but false state nor unjustified true
belief as a distinct true but epistemically bad state; both are forced
into the single residual category of 'mere belief'. This is why a richer
taxonomy of justified/unjustified and true/false is required even apart
from Gettier.

2.text:
With JTB Knowledge = Justified ∧ True ∧ Belief the 2 × 2 table of Truth × Justification is

* J ∧ T → Knowledge
* J ∧ ¬T → ?
* ¬J ∧ T → ?
* ¬J ∧ ¬T → ?

With only two epistemic kinds to put things in, Knowledge and Belief, the ? cells cannot be given their own kind. Knowledge is closed under truth, so the J ∧ ¬T cell can never be Knowledge. The ¬J ∧ T cell can never be Knowledge because it is unjustified. The ¬J ∧ ¬T cell can never be Knowledge for the same reason.

Hence the whole residual category Belief is forced to be the catch-all for

* Justified False Belief
* Unjustified True Belief
* Unjustified False Belief

i.e. for everything that is not Justified True Belief.

That gives the two familiar coarse-graining costs.

1. Justified error has no home. A belief that is in fact false but is held on good, adequate grounds is not Knowledge because it is false, and with only Knowledge and Belief available it has to be called a mere Belief. Belief is therefore made to cover justified falsehood as well as unjustified falsehood. The distinct epistemic standing of a justified, though false, belief is lost.

2. Lucky true belief has no home. A belief that is in fact true but is held without any justification is not Knowledge because it is unjustified, and with only Knowledge and Belief available it has to be called a mere Belief. Belief is therefore made to cover justified truehood as well as unjustified truehood. The distinct epistemic standing of an unjustified, though true, belief is lost.

In effect Belief becomes a disjunctive, heterogeneous grab-bag of J∧¬T, ¬J∧T and ¬J∧¬T, while Knowledge is the single cell J∧T. Justification and truth are no longer tracked inside the belief state, so the taxonomy is too coarse to mark justified false belief and unjustified true belief as different from one another and from knowledge. That is the forced collapse that makes belief epistemically vacuous.

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: With only Knowledge and Belief as epistemic states available for the Justification condition, the justification of any candidate belief p has to be either a piece of knowledge or a mere belief.

If you try to meet justification by invoking a further belief that supports p, that supporting belief itself needs justification. That justification can only be supplied by yet another belief, and so on. You get an infinite regress of justifiers with no terminating ground, so you never actually secure a justified true belief in the first place.

The alternative stop the chain is to allow some beliefs to be justified without themselves being justified. On a knowledge-only menu that means you are forced to treat some beliefs as brute, dogmatically basic, and ultimately arbitrary starting points. Knowledge then rests on unjustified beliefs, which is at odds with the demand that knowledge be justified. So JTB is left with either an endless regress of justification or an arbitrary foundational halt.

14.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: With JTB the justificatory condition is what does the work, and on the stated inventory that condition immediately generates a regress problem. To count a belief p as justified you need some further proposition q that justifies p. If q is itself a belief, then q must in turn be justified by r, and so on. Since the only epistemic statuses we allow are Knowledge and Belief, and a belief is not yet knowledge unless it is already justified and true, the chain cannot be absorbed at an intermediate belief without re-triggering the justification requirement. That is the familiar regress of reasons.

The only way to block the regress is to stop it somewhere. With only Knowledge and Belief available there is no third, properly basic epistemic status to cash out a non-arbitrary stopping point. You can either keep going forever, or you are forced to arbitrarily privilege a set of beliefs as justified simpliciter – i.e., to treat some beliefs as foundationally immune from further justification. That is an arbitrary dogmatism about where justification is allowed to terminate: we are left either with an infinite justificatory chain or with an ungrounded, stipulative choice of which beliefs are taken as the base, so that the justificatory apparatus never gets off the ground in a non-question-begging way.

12.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: With JTB the classification of a doxastic item is fixed by truth T/F and justification J/U.

T+J = Knowledge
T+U, F+J, F+U = not knowledge

If the only epistemic labels you are allowed to use are Knowledge and Belief, then everything that is not Knowledge has to be called Belief. That makes Belief a heterogeneous catch-all.

* F+J : Justified false belief. It is not Knowledge because it is false, so by hypothesis it must be a mere Belief. There is now no label for a belief that is justified but false, so justified false belief is lumped together with unjustified false belief. Justification is thereby lost inside the Belief box.

* T+U : Unjustified true belief. It is not Knowledge because it is unjustified, so by hypothesis it must be a mere Belief. There is now no label for a true belief that is unjustified, so unjustified true belief is lumped together with false belief, justified or not. Truth is thereby lost inside the Belief box.

Hence Belief as defined has to contain both true and false items and both justified and unjustified items. In particular you cannot distinguish a justified false belief from an unjustified false belief, and you cannot distinguish an unjustified true belief from a false belief. The two unclassifiable cases the two-state scheme forces into Belief are the justified false belief and the unjustified true belief, which is why the plain JTB scheme is normally supplemented with further epistemic states such as justified belief, true belief, warranted belief, etc.

6.text:
Under JTB the classification is by truth and justification

* T & J & B = Knowledge
* ¬T or ¬J or ¬B = not Knowledge

If the only place you have to put a non-K state is Belief then the
four truth/justification cells collapse into two labels.

T J
T ¬J
¬T J
¬T ¬J

The first cell is Knowledge by JTB. The other three cells are all
forced to be “mere belief”. That makes Belief a heterogeneous grab bag
and you lose grade discrimination in two places.

* Justified false belief. ¬T & J & B. By JTB it is not knowledge because
it is false, so on the two-state taxonomy it is just a Belief. Justified
false belief is therefore indistinguishable in kind from an
unjustified false belief. Justification is invisible inside the
Belief class and a belief that is epistemically well supported is
classified in the same box as a belief that is epistemically
unsupported.

* Unjustified true belief. T & ¬J & B. By JTB it is not knowledge
because it is unjustified, so on the two-state taxonomy it is just a
Belief. Unjustified true belief is therefore indistinguishable in kind
from an unjustified false belief. Truth is invisible inside the Belief
class and a true belief is classified in the same box as a false belief.

Hence Belief comes to mean “anything that is not justified true belief”,
i.e. justified false belief, true unjustified belief and false
unjustified belief all together. The JTB partition cannot respect the
intuitive epistemic improvement conferred by justification on its own,
and the intuitive improvement conferred by truth on its own, because
with only Knowledge and Belief as labels both of those improvements are
swallowed up in mere Belief. That is the classic justified-false-belief
and the classic unjustified-true-belief, or lucky-true-belief, problem
for JTB.

13.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Under a JTB constraint the justification condition is the trouble spot. If the only epistemic attitudes we are allowed to appeal to are belief and knowledge, then any attempt to justify a target belief p has to appeal to something else that is either a belief or a piece of knowledge.

If you try to justify p by another belief q, q itself needs a justification, and then whatever justifies q needs a justification, and so on. That is the familiar regress of justification: you never reach a terminus, you just keep pushing the need for a further justifier back indefinitely.

The alternative is to stop the chain. The only way to stop without invoking a third epistemic status such as warrant, entitlement or a properly basic belief is to insist that some belief or piece of knowledge is justified in itself, i.e. to treat it as dogmatically basic. With the state space restricted to Knowledge and Belief that amounts to having to posit an arbitrary, ungrounded stopping point – a basic belief/knowledge that is taken as justified simply because we have to stop somewhere. That is the dogmatic/foundational stopping-point problem that is the second horn of the Münchhausen trilemma in this setting. In practice JTB is therefore forced either into an endless regress of justifiers or into an unmotivated, arbitrarily basic belief/knowledge.

5.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: On the JTB picture K p iff J p & T p & B p, Knowledge is factive and
belief-involving. If the only doxastic categories you have to work with are
K and B then B is simply “not-K”. That makes B a heterogeneous catch-all.

* Justification is not guaranteed by truth. In a two-state system a belief
that is justified but false is still just a B. JTB therefore has to allow
justified false belief: you can be for good reasons committed to p, J p hold,
and p be false, and the state of the agent is still only Belief, not
Knowledge. Justification is thus decoupled from truth.

* Truth is not guaranteed by justification. In a two-state system a belief
that is true but unjustified is still just a B. JTB therefore has to allow
true belief without justification, i.e. epistemic luck. A lucky guess, a
Meno true opinion, is T p & B p & ~J p and it counts as mere Belief, not
Knowledge. Truth is thus decoupled from justification.

With only Knowledge and Belief at your disposal Belief has to do double
duty for both justified false beliefs and for true but unjustified beliefs.
That is why Belief is not sufficient for Knowledge and why JTB has to keep a
separate justification condition to move from the coarse-grained B-state to
the factive K-state. The familiar Gettier worry is set aside, the
underlying underdetermination remains: justification can mislead you into
false belief and truth can be had by accident without justification, and in
a Knowledge/Belief only taxonomy both cases look just like Belief.

11.text:
With JTB knowledge is a species of belief. Knowledge = B(p) & True(p) & J(p). 
If the taxonomy you are allowed to use is just

* Knowledge
* Belief

then the justification and truth dimensions are not independently
trackable as epistemic states, they are only visible as the presence or
absence of Knowledge.

Hence the 2x2 matrix of Truth x Justification collapses.

* Justified, False, Believed.  JTB says this is not knowledge because
¬True(p). On the Knowledge/Belief taxonomy it has to be filed as mere
Belief. So a justified false belief and an unjustified false belief are
indistinguishable. The account loses the epistemic merit of being
justified in the face of falsity. In ordinary talk we want to say a
justified false belief is epistemically better than an unjustified false
belief, but JTB gives them the same label.

* True, Unjustified, Believed. JTB says this is not knowledge because
¬J(p). On the Knowledge/Belief taxonomy it also has to be filed as mere
Belief. So an unjustified true belief, e.g. a lucky guess, a true
coincidence, is indistinguishable from an unjustified false belief and
from a justified false belief. The account loses the epistemic merit of
truth in the absence of justification.

In effect JTB, with only Knowledge and Belief as available states, has
no room for a distinct epistemic category of justified belief at all
and no room for a distinct category of true but unjustified belief. The
virtues of justification and truth can only be recorded together as
Knowledge, everything else is just “Belief”. That is why we normally
want intermediate states such as justified belief and unjustified true
belief, or a separate value for justification, once Gettier worries are
put aside.

15.text:
With JTB

K = Justified  & True  & Belief

and with only the two doxastic categories K and B = not-K you get

B = not [Justified & True & Belief]
  = [¬Justified ∨ ¬True ∨ ¬Belief] & Belief
  = ¬Justified & Belief ∨ ¬True & Belief

i.e. everything that is a belief but fails knowledge. That class is
heterogeneous.

* Justified False Belief.  J ∧ ¬T ∧ B.  It fails the truth condition so
it is not K. With only K/B available it has to be put in B. So B is
justified. A justified belief can be false and it is still merely a
belief. The truth condition therefore does not protect justification
and the category Belief now contains justified items.

* Unjustified True Belief.  ¬J ∧ T ∧ B.  It fails the justification
condition so it is not K. With only K/B available it has to be put in B.
So B is true. A true belief can be unjustified and it is still merely a
belief. The justification condition therefore does not guarantee truth
and the category Belief now contains true items.

Hence on a strict K/B dichotomy Belief is not the uniform opposite of
Knowledge. It is the disjunction of justified false beliefs and true
unjustified beliefs – indeed of all ¬J∧B, ¬T∧B and ¬J∧¬T∧B – so the
binary taxonomy loses its discriminatory power. Knowledge is a proper
subset of Belief, Belief is both sometimes justified and sometimes true,
and there is no place to put a justified false belief and an
unjustified true belief except in the undifferentiated residual class
Belief. That is the familiar JFB and UTB gaps which make a pure K vs B
ontology incoherent, apart from Gettier.

10.text:
With JTB the 2x2 truth / justification matrix is forced into the two
boxes Knowledge = JTB and Belief = everything else.

Truth  Justified       Unjustified
True        Knowledge   Unjustified true belief
False       Justified false belief   Unjustified false belief

If the only epistemic kinds you allow are Knowledge and Belief then
the two off-diagonal cells have nowhere to go.

* Justified false belief. A belief can be rationally justified and
still be false. On JTB it is not Knowledge because the truth condition
fails. On the two-state taxonomy it has to be classified as mere
Belief, i.e. its justification is lost in the classification. A
justified false belief is not just a belief in the ordinary
unjustified sense, yet JTB has no place for it.

* Unjustified true belief. A belief can be true by accident or luck
and still lack justification. On JTB it is not Knowledge because the
justification condition fails. On the two-state taxonomy it still has
to be classified as mere Belief, i.e. its truth is lost in the
classification. An unjustified true belief is not just a belief in the
ordinary false or unjustified sense, yet JTB has no place for it.

Hence with only Knowledge and Belief as live categories JTB is forced
to lump justified false beliefs together with unjustified false beliefs
and unjustified true beliefs together with unjustified false beliefs.
The four natural epistemic statuses of justified/true, justified/false,
unjustified/true and unjustified/false collapse into the two
coarse-grained boxes Knowledge vs Belief and the information carried
by justification alone and by truth alone is lost. That is the
over-generation/under-generation that remains even apart from Gettier
cases.

4.text:
Under a strictly two state ontology justification has nowhere to live.

* Justification is not Knowledge and it is not Belief. If a belief p is
to count as justified its justification must itself be entertained in the
only states you allow, i.e. as a belief or as knowledge.  If the
justifying state is itself a belief that is itself to be justified you
get the familiar trilemma for the source of justification.

Either the justifying beliefs are themselves justified and you get an
infinite regress of ever-further beliefs/knowledge needed to justify the
justifiers, or you stop the regress with some beliefs that are held
without justification, i.e. dogmatism, or you close the series back on
itself and get vicious epistemic circularity. In a Knowledge/Belief only
ontology there is no independent justified-belief state in which the
justification can be parked.

Because of that the epistemic work that the J-word is supposed to do
collapses into the Belief category. 

1. Justified false belief. A belief can be well-supported and still be
false. On JTB it is not Knowledge because it is not true, and on a
Knowledge/Belief only taxonomy it is just a Belief. The fact that it is
justified therefore makes no difference to its official epistemic kind.
Justification is hence invisible for false beliefs.

2. Unjustified true belief. A belief can be true by accident and lack
any support at all. On JTB it is not Knowledge because it is not
justified, and on a Knowledge/Belief only taxonomy it is just a Belief.
The fact that it is unjustified therefore makes no difference to its
official epistemic kind. The JTB account therefore cannot mark the
intuitive distinction between a justified true belief, which is supposed
to be Knowledge, and an unjustified true belief, which is supposed to
remain mere true belief, nor between a justified false belief and a
mere false belief.

That is why the traditional move is to posit a third, intermediate
epistemic state, justified belief/warrant, rather than try to squeeze
justification into Knowledge and Belief alone.  Ignoring Gettier, this is
the regress/circularity problem for the location of justification and the
collapse of the justified vs unjustified distinction within the bare
Belief category.

9.text:
Assume JTB there are in principle four different doxastic-combinations of the
two dimensions belief / no belief and true / false with or without a
justificatory warrant.

* T+J+B = Knowledge
* T+~J+B = true but unjustified belief
* ~T+J+B = justified false belief
* ~T+~J+B = false unjustified belief

On the JTB analysis the first cell is Knowledge and the three remaining
cells are not Knowledge. If the doxastic taxonomy you are allowed to use is
only Knowledge / Belief then everything that is not Knowledge is forced
into the single category Belief. The tripartite analysis therefore becomes
coarse-grained in exactly two places.

First, the justification of error is lost. Both ~T+J+B and ~T+~J+B are
just Belief. There is no epistemic state in which to locate a justified
false belief, a belief that is epistemically responsible even though it is
wrong, and it is therefore indistinguishable from a plain, unjustified
false belief. We can no longer credit a subject for being justified when
she is mistaken.

Second, luck is not marked off from justified error. Both T+~J+B and
~T+J+B are just Belief. A true belief that is held by accident, that is
unjustified and true, is lumped together with a belief that is justified
and false. The two very different normative situations of “right for the
wrong reason’’ and “wrong for the right reason’’ become epistemically
identical, and there is no place to say that an unjustified true belief
remains only belief whereas a justified false belief is at least an
epistemically good belief.

That is the loss of granularity you get when justification is not itself
allowed a state. In effect justification can only show up as the
difference between Knowledge and Belief, i.e. as the difference maker for
true belief.  With only Knowledge and Belief as primitive states that
forces either circularity – justification is then analysed in terms of
knowledge so that *K = J T B* is circular – or a regress – justification is
analysed in terms of belief so that being justified in believing P requires
being justified in believing the beliefs that justify P, etc.  The
coarse-grained taxonomy is the familiar statement of the problem in
extensional terms.

8.text:
With the JTB analysis the logically possible positions in the justification/truth
matrix are

* J T  -> Knowledge on JTB
* J F  -> 
* U T  -> 
* U F  -> 

If the only epistemic kinds you are allowed to name are Knowledge and Belief
the three non-JTB cells have to be put under the single label Belief.

Hence the 2×2 is collapsed into

Knowledge = J T
Belief = J F  ∨  U T  ∨  U F .

That collapse removes the two independently intelligible epistemic
positions that the matrix makes room for.

1. Justified false belief. J F is not knowledge because it is not true, so
on the binary taxonomy it is just a Belief.  So justified belief is made
epistemically indistinguishable from an unjustified false belief. In
effect justification makes no difference to the status of a false
proposition: a well justified mistake and a baseless mistake are both just
‘belief’. Justification therefore does not guarantee truth and the
justification condition is idle for the false case.

2. Unjustified true belief. U T is not knowledge because it is not
justified, so on the binary taxonomy it is also just a Belief. So a true
proposition is made epistemically indistinguishable from a justified false
proposition. In effect truth makes no difference to the status of a
non-knowledge belief: a lucky true guess and a justified falsehood are
both just ‘belief’. Truth therefore does not guarantee knowledge and the
truth condition is idle for the non-knowledge case.

In practice this is the familiar justification-without-truth / truth-without-
justification gap. There is no room in a Knowledge/Belief only ontology for
a properly justified but mistaken belief, nor for a true belief that is
true only by luck. JTB is therefore forced to treat all three non-JTB
combinations as the same unarticulated epistemic state, ‘mere belief’. That
is the loss of granularity that makes the account implausible apart from
the Gettier cases.

3.text:
The JTB schema needs a notion of justified belief which is independent of
truth. Knowledge on the JTB picture is

* JTB = K
* B & ~J = B
* J & ~T = B
* ~J & ~T = B

i.e. the only way for justification to show up in the taxonomy is as the
difference between K and B. If the only epistemic attitudes you are
allowed to name are K and B there is no place to put justified belief as
such.

That means that justification can only be exhibited by the two states
you have. In effect justification is then either

* K-based, or 
* B-based.

If a justified belief is justified by another belief you need a
justification for the justifier, and so on. With only B and K in the menu
you get the familiar regress of justification for justification.

If a justified belief is justified by a piece of knowledge you get
knowledge used in the analysis of knowledge. A belief is justified iff it
is justified by something the agent knows, so that to have a justified
true belief you already have to know the justifiers. Justification is
then truth- and knowledge-dependent and the justification condition is
circular.

In the static taxonomy this shows up as the loss of the two intermediate
cells of the truth x justification matrix. Justified false belief and
unjustified true belief are both, by the JTB taxonomy, just B, so that
you can no longer mark

* J & ~T : a justified false belief, a belief that is epistemically
  good even though it is false, as distinct from an unjustified false
  belief; and

* ~J & T : an unjustified true belief, a true belief that is
  epistemically bad because it is lucky, as distinct from a justified
  true belief.

With only K and B at your disposal justified belief is either identified
with knowledge when it is true and collapses into mere belief when it is
false, so justification ceases to be an independent epistemic
explanans and you are left with the regress/circularity of the
justification condition. That is why the JTB picture is normally
supplemented by a distinct attitude of justified belief, and with the
two-attitude menu you lose it.

With JTB the justificatory condition is what does the work, and on the stated inventory that condition immediately generates a regress problem. To count a belief p as justified you need some further proposition q that justifies p. If q is itself a belief, then q must in turn be justified by r, and so on. Since the only epistemic statuses we allow are Knowledge and Belief, and a belief is not yet knowledge unless it is already justified and true, the chain cannot be absorbed at an intermediate belief without re-triggering the justification requirement. That is the familiar regress of reasons.

The only way to block the regress is to stop it somewhere. With only Knowledge and Belief available there is no third, properly basic epistemic status to cash out a non-arbitrary stopping point. You can either keep going forever, or you are forced to arbitrarily privilege a set of beliefs as justified simpliciter – i.e., to treat some beliefs as foundationally immune from further justification. That is an arbitrary dogmatism about where justification is allowed to terminate: we are left either with an infinite justificatory chain or with an ungrounded, stipulative choice of which beliefs are taken as the base, so that the justificatory apparatus never gets off the ground in a non-question-begging way.
public_text.12:
With JTB the classification of a doxastic item is fixed by truth T/F and justification J/U.

T+J = Knowledge
T+U, F+J, F+U = not knowledge

If the only epistemic labels you are allowed to use are Knowledge and Belief, then everything that is not Knowledge has to be called Belief. That makes Belief a heterogeneous catch-all.

* F+J : Justified false belief. It is not Knowledge because it is false, so by hypothesis it must be a mere Belief. There is now no label for a belief that is justified but false, so justified false belief is lumped together with unjustified false belief. Justification is thereby lost inside the Belief box.

* T+U : Unjustified true belief. It is not Knowledge because it is unjustified, so by hypothesis it must be a mere Belief. There is now no label for a true belief that is unjustified, so unjustified true belief is lumped together with false belief, justified or not. Truth is thereby lost inside the Belief box.

Hence Belief as defined has to contain both true and false items and both justified and unjustified items. In particular you cannot distinguish a justified false belief from an unjustified false belief, and you cannot distinguish an unjustified true belief from a false belief. The two unclassifiable cases the two-state scheme forces into Belief are the justified false belief and the unjustified true belief, which is why the plain JTB scheme is normally supplemented with further epistemic states such as justified belief, true belief, warranted belief, etc.
public_text.6:
Under JTB the classification is by truth and justification

* T & J & B = Knowledge
* ¬T or ¬J or ¬B = not Knowledge

If the only place you have to put a non-K state is Belief then the
four truth/justification cells collapse into two labels.

T J
T ¬J
¬T J
¬T ¬J

The first cell is Knowledge by JTB. The other three cells are all
forced to be “mere belief”. That makes Belief a heterogeneous grab bag
and you lose grade discrimination in two places.

* Justified false belief. ¬T & J & B. By JTB it is not knowledge because
it is false, so on the two-state taxonomy it is just a Belief. Justified
false belief is therefore indistinguishable in kind from an
unjustified false belief. Justification is invisible inside the
Belief class and a belief that is epistemically well supported is
classified in the same box as a belief that is epistemically
unsupported.

* Unjustified true belief. T & ¬J & B. By JTB it is not knowledge
because it is unjustified, so on the two-state taxonomy it is just a
Belief. Unjustified true belief is therefore indistinguishable in kind
from an unjustified false belief. Truth is invisible inside the Belief
class and a true belief is classified in the same box as a false belief.

Hence Belief comes to mean “anything that is not justified true belief”,
i.e. justified false belief, true unjustified belief and false
unjustified belief all together. The JTB partition cannot respect the
intuitive epistemic improvement conferred by justification on its own,
and the intuitive improvement conferred by truth on its own, because
with only Knowledge and Belief as labels both of those improvements are
swallowed up in mere Belief. That is the classic justified-false-belief
and the classic unjustified-true-belief, or lucky-true-belief, problem
for JTB.
public_text.13:
Under a JTB constraint the justification condition is the trouble spot. If the only epistemic attitudes we are allowed to appeal to are belief and knowledge, then any attempt to justify a target belief p has to appeal to something else that is either a belief or a piece of knowledge.

If you try to justify p by another belief q, q itself needs a justification, and then whatever justifies q needs a justification, and so on. That is the familiar regress of justification: you never reach a terminus, you just keep pushing the need for a further justifier back indefinitely.

The alternative is to stop the chain. The only way to stop without invoking a third epistemic status such as warrant, entitlement or a properly basic belief is to insist that some belief or piece of knowledge is justified in itself, i.e. to treat it as dogmatically basic. With the state space restricted to Knowledge and Belief that amounts to having to posit an arbitrary, ungrounded stopping point – a basic belief/knowledge that is taken as justified simply because we have to stop somewhere. That is the dogmatic/foundational stopping-point problem that is the second horn of the Münchhausen trilemma in this setting. In practice JTB is therefore forced either into an endless regress of justifiers or into an unmotivated, arbitrarily basic belief/knowledge.
public_text.5:
On the JTB picture K p iff J p & T p & B p, Knowledge is factive and
belief-involving. If the only doxastic categories you have to work with are
K and B then B is simply “not-K”. That makes B a heterogeneous catch-all.

* Justification is not guaranteed by truth. In a two-state system a belief
that is justified but false is still just a B. JTB therefore has to allow
justified false belief: you can be for good reasons committed to p, J p hold,
and p be false, and the state of the agent is still only Belief, not
Knowledge. Justification is thus decoupled from truth.

* Truth is not guaranteed by justification. In a two-state system a belief
that is true but unjustified is still just a B. JTB therefore has to allow
true belief without justification, i.e. epistemic luck. A lucky guess, a
Meno true opinion, is T p & B p & ~J p and it counts as mere Belief, not
Knowledge. Truth is thus decoupled from justification.

With only Knowledge and Belief at your disposal Belief has to do double
duty for both justified false beliefs and for true but unjustified beliefs.
That is why Belief is not sufficient for Knowledge and why JTB has to keep a
separate justification condition to move from the coarse-grained B-state to
the factive K-state. The familiar Gettier worry is set aside, the
underlying underdetermination remains: justification can mislead you into
false belief and truth can be had by accident without justification, and in
a Knowledge/Belief only taxonomy both cases look just like Belief.
public_text.11:
With JTB knowledge is a species of belief. Knowledge = B(p) & True(p) & J(p). 
If the taxonomy you are allowed to use is just

* Knowledge
* Belief

then the justification and truth dimensions are not independently
trackable as epistemic states, they are only visible as the presence or
absence of Knowledge.

Hence the 2x2 matrix of Truth x Justification collapses.

* Justified, False, Believed.  JTB says this is not knowledge because
¬True(p). On the Knowledge/Belief taxonomy it has to be filed as mere
Belief. So a justified false belief and an unjustified false belief are
indistinguishable. The account loses the epistemic merit of being
justified in the face of falsity. In ordinary talk we want to say a
justified false belief is epistemically better than an unjustified false
belief, but JTB gives them the same label.

* True, Unjustified, Believed. JTB says this is not knowledge because
¬J(p). On the Knowledge/Belief taxonomy it also has to be filed as mere
Belief. So an unjustified true belief, e.g. a lucky guess, a true
coincidence, is indistinguishable from an unjustified false belief and
from a justified false belief. The account loses the epistemic merit of
truth in the absence of justification.

In effect JTB, with only Knowledge and Belief as available states, has
no room for a distinct epistemic category of justified belief at all
and no room for a distinct category of true but unjustified belief. The
virtues of justification and truth can only be recorded together as
Knowledge, everything else is just “Belief”. That is why we normally
want intermediate states such as justified belief and unjustified true
belief, or a separate value for justification, once Gettier worries are
put aside.
public_text.15:
With JTB

K = Justified  & True  & Belief

and with only the two doxastic categories K and B = not-K you get

B = not [Justified & True & Belief]
  = [¬Justified ∨ ¬True ∨ ¬Belief] & Belief
  = ¬Justified & Belief ∨ ¬True & Belief

i.e. everything that is a belief but fails knowledge. That class is
heterogeneous.

* Justified False Belief.  J ∧ ¬T ∧ B.  It fails the truth condition so
it is not K. With only K/B available it has to be put in B. So B is
justified. A justified belief can be false and it is still merely a
belief. The truth condition therefore does not protect justification
and the category Belief now contains justified items.

* Unjustified True Belief.  ¬J ∧ T ∧ B.  It fails the justification
condition so it is not K. With only K/B available it has to be put in B.
So B is true. A true belief can be unjustified and it is still merely a
belief. The justification condition therefore does not guarantee truth
and the category Belief now contains true items.

Hence on a strict K/B dichotomy Belief is not the uniform opposite of
Knowledge. It is the disjunction of justified false beliefs and true
unjustified beliefs – indeed of all ¬J∧B, ¬T∧B and ¬J∧¬T∧B – so the
binary taxonomy loses its discriminatory power. Knowledge is a proper
subset of Belief, Belief is both sometimes justified and sometimes true,
and there is no place to put a justified false belief and an
unjustified true belief except in the undifferentiated residual class
Belief. That is the familiar JFB and UTB gaps which make a pure K vs B
ontology incoherent, apart from Gettier.
public_text.10:
With JTB the 2x2 truth / justification matrix is forced into the two
boxes Knowledge = JTB and Belief = everything else.

Truth  Justified       Unjustified
True        Knowledge   Unjustified true belief
False       Justified false belief   Unjustified false belief

If the only epistemic kinds you allow are Knowledge and Belief then
the two off-diagonal cells have nowhere to go.

* Justified false belief. A belief can be rationally justified and
still be false. On JTB it is not Knowledge because the truth condition
fails. On the two-state taxonomy it has to be classified as mere
Belief, i.e. its justification is lost in the classification. A
justified false belief is not just a belief in the ordinary
unjustified sense, yet JTB has no place for it.

* Unjustified true belief. A belief can be true by accident or luck
and still lack justification. On JTB it is not Knowledge because the
justification condition fails. On the two-state taxonomy it still has
to be classified as mere Belief, i.e. its truth is lost in the
classification. An unjustified true belief is not just a belief in the
ordinary false or unjustified sense, yet JTB has no place for it.

Hence with only Knowledge and Belief as live categories JTB is forced
to lump justified false beliefs together with unjustified false beliefs
and unjustified true beliefs together with unjustified false beliefs.
The four natural epistemic statuses of justified/true, justified/false,
unjustified/true and unjustified/false collapse into the two
coarse-grained boxes Knowledge vs Belief and the information carried
by justification alone and by truth alone is lost. That is the
over-generation/under-generation that remains even apart from Gettier
cases.
public_text.4:
Under a strictly two state ontology justification has nowhere to live.

* Justification is not Knowledge and it is not Belief. If a belief p is
to count as justified its justification must itself be entertained in the
only states you allow, i.e. as a belief or as knowledge.  If the
justifying state is itself a belief that is itself to be justified you
get the familiar trilemma for the source of justification.

Either the justifying beliefs are themselves justified and you get an
infinite regress of ever-further beliefs/knowledge needed to justify the
justifiers, or you stop the regress with some beliefs that are held
without justification, i.e. dogmatism, or you close the series back on
itself and get vicious epistemic circularity. In a Knowledge/Belief only
ontology there is no independent justified-belief state in which the
justification can be parked.

Because of that the epistemic work that the J-word is supposed to do
collapses into the Belief category. 

1. Justified false belief. A belief can be well-supported and still be
false. On JTB it is not Knowledge because it is not true, and on a
Knowledge/Belief only taxonomy it is just a Belief. The fact that it is
justified therefore makes no difference to its official epistemic kind.
Justification is hence invisible for false beliefs.

2. Unjustified true belief. A belief can be true by accident and lack
any support at all. On JTB it is not Knowledge because it is not
justified, and on a Knowledge/Belief only taxonomy it is just a Belief.
The fact that it is unjustified therefore makes no difference to its
official epistemic kind. The JTB account therefore cannot mark the
intuitive distinction between a justified true belief, which is supposed
to be Knowledge, and an unjustified true belief, which is supposed to
remain mere true belief, nor between a justified false belief and a
mere false belief.

That is why the traditional move is to posit a third, intermediate
epistemic state, justified belief/warrant, rather than try to squeeze
justification into Knowledge and Belief alone.  Ignoring Gettier, this is
the regress/circularity problem for the location of justification and the
collapse of the justified vs unjustified distinction within the bare
Belief category.
public_text.9:
Assume JTB there are in principle four different doxastic-combinations of the
two dimensions belief / no belief and true / false with or without a
justificatory warrant.

* T+J+B = Knowledge
* T+~J+B = true but unjustified belief
* ~T+J+B = justified false belief
* ~T+~J+B = false unjustified belief

On the JTB analysis the first cell is Knowledge and the three remaining
cells are not Knowledge. If the doxastic taxonomy you are allowed to use is
only Knowledge / Belief then everything that is not Knowledge is forced
into the single category Belief. The tripartite analysis therefore becomes
coarse-grained in exactly two places.

First, the justification of error is lost. Both ~T+J+B and ~T+~J+B are
just Belief. There is no epistemic state in which to locate a justified
false belief, a belief that is epistemically responsible even though it is
wrong, and it is therefore indistinguishable from a plain, unjustified
false belief. We can no longer credit a subject for being justified when
she is mistaken.

Second, luck is not marked off from justified error. Both T+~J+B and
~T+J+B are just Belief. A true belief that is held by accident, that is
unjustified and true, is lumped together with a belief that is justified
and false. The two very different normative situations of “right for the
wrong reason’’ and “wrong for the right reason’’ become epistemically
identical, and there is no place to say that an unjustified true belief
remains only belief whereas a justified false belief is at least an
epistemically good belief.

That is the loss of granularity you get when justification is not itself
allowed a state. In effect justification can only show up as the
difference between Knowledge and Belief, i.e. as the difference maker for
true belief.  With only Knowledge and Belief as primitive states that
forces either circularity – justification is then analysed in terms of
knowledge so that *K = J T B* is circular – or a regress – justification is
analysed in terms of belief so that being justified in believing P requires
being justified in believing the beliefs that justify P, etc.  The
coarse-grained taxonomy is the familiar statement of the problem in
extensional terms.
public_text.8:
With the JTB analysis the logically possible positions in the justification/truth
matrix are

* J T  -> Knowledge on JTB
* J F  -> 
* U T  -> 
* U F  -> 

If the only epistemic kinds you are allowed to name are Knowledge and Belief
the three non-JTB cells have to be put under the single label Belief.

Hence the 2×2 is collapsed into

Knowledge = J T
Belief = J F  ∨  U T  ∨  U F .

That collapse removes the two independently intelligible epistemic
positions that the matrix makes room for.

1. Justified false belief. J F is not knowledge because it is not true, so
on the binary taxonomy it is just a Belief.  So justified belief is made
epistemically indistinguishable from an unjustified false belief. In
effect justification makes no difference to the status of a false
proposition: a well justified mistake and a baseless mistake are both just
‘belief’. Justification therefore does not guarantee truth and the
justification condition is idle for the false case.

2. Unjustified true belief. U T is not knowledge because it is not
justified, so on the binary taxonomy it is also just a Belief. So a true
proposition is made epistemically indistinguishable from a justified false
proposition. In effect truth makes no difference to the status of a
non-knowledge belief: a lucky true guess and a justified falsehood are
both just ‘belief’. Truth therefore does not guarantee knowledge and the
truth condition is idle for the non-knowledge case.

In practice this is the familiar justification-without-truth / truth-without-
justification gap. There is no room in a Knowledge/Belief only ontology for
a properly justified but mistaken belief, nor for a true belief that is
true only by luck. JTB is therefore forced to treat all three non-JTB
combinations as the same unarticulated epistemic state, ‘mere belief’. That
is the loss of granularity that makes the account implausible apart from
the Gettier cases.
public_text.3:
The JTB schema needs a notion of justified belief which is independent of
truth. Knowledge on the JTB picture is

* JTB = K
* B & ~J = B
* J & ~T = B
* ~J & ~T = B

i.e. the only way for justification to show up in the taxonomy is as the
difference between K and B. If the only epistemic attitudes you are
allowed to name are K and B there is no place to put justified belief as
such.

That means that justification can only be exhibited by the two states
you have. In effect justification is then either

* K-based, or 
* B-based.

If a justified belief is justified by another belief you need a
justification for the justifier, and so on. With only B and K in the menu
you get the familiar regress of justification for justification.

If a justified belief is justified by a piece of knowledge you get
knowledge used in the analysis of knowledge. A belief is justified iff it
is justified by something the agent knows, so that to have a justified
true belief you already have to know the justifiers. Justification is
then truth- and knowledge-dependent and the justification condition is
circular.

In the static taxonomy this shows up as the loss of the two intermediate
cells of the truth x justification matrix. Justified false belief and
unjustified true belief are both, by the JTB taxonomy, just B, so that
you can no longer mark

* J & ~T : a justified false belief, a belief that is epistemically
  good even though it is false, as distinct from an unjustified false
  belief; and

* ~J & T : an unjustified true belief, a true belief that is
  epistemically bad because it is lucky, as distinct from a justified
  true belief.

With only K and B at your disposal justified belief is either identified
with knowledge when it is true and collapses into mere belief when it is
false, so justification ceases to be an independent epistemic
explanans and you are left with the regress/circularity of the
justification condition. That is why the JTB picture is normally
supplemented by a distinct attitude of justified belief, and with the
two-attitude menu you lose it.

2.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The round-0 discussion converges on the coarse-graining that follows from restricting the ontology to Knowledge = Justified True Belief and Belief = ¬Knowledge.

With JTB the Truth × Justification matrix is T,J ; T,¬J ; ¬T,J ; ¬T,¬J. On JTB only the T,J cell is Knowledge. If the only labels allowed are Knowledge and Belief, then B is defined as ¬K, i.e. B = ¬J∧T ∨ J∧¬T ∨ ¬J∧¬T. Belief therefore becomes a heterogeneous catch-all.

The dominant claim across most colleagues 1,2,6,8,10,11,12,15 is that this collapse loses independent tracking of justification and truth:

* Justified false belief, J∧¬T∧B. It fails truth so it is not Knowledge, but on a two-state taxonomy it must be filed as mere Belief. Hence a justified error is indistinguishable from an unjustified false belief and from an unjustified true belief. Justification is invisible for false beliefs; a well-supported mistake and a baseless mistake share the same epistemic kind.

* Unjustified true belief, ¬J∧T∧B. It fails justification so it is not Knowledge, but on a two-state taxonomy it must also be filed as mere Belief. Hence a lucky true belief is indistinguishable from a justified false belief and from an unjustified false belief. Truth is invisible inside the Belief class; a true belief by accident and a false belief by accident share the same epistemic kind.

In effect Belief has to do double duty for both justified falsehoods and true-but-unjustified beliefs, so the virtues of justification on its own and truth on its own can only be recorded together as Knowledge. That is the familiar JFB and UTB gaps apart from Gettier.

A minority thread – colleagues 13,14,4,7,3 – stresses the internal justificatory structure: with only Knowledge and Belief to do the work of justification, justification of p must appeal to q which is either Knowledge or Belief. If belief, the regress of justifiers re-arises; if knowledge, justification becomes circular/knowledge-dependent. This yields the trilemma of regress, dogmatic foundational stopping point, or circularity for the justification condition when no distinct justified-belief state is available.

I am retaining the consensus coarse-graining problems – loss of a distinct status for justified false belief and for unjustified true belief – as the core answer, while noting the regress/dogmatism concern as a related structural worry about how justification can be located at all on a Knowledge/Belief only menu. Unresolved is whether the question intends the two off-diagonal classification problems or the classification problem plus the justificatory regress problem.

1.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The round-0 discussion converges on the coarse-graining that a Knowledge/Belief-only ontology forces on the JTB tripartite analysis K = B & J & T.

With only K and B = ¬K the Truth × Justification 2x2 collapses to:
* J∧T → Knowledge
* J∧¬T, ¬J∧T, ¬J∧¬T → all forced into the single residual label ‘mere Belief’.

The majority view is that this makes Belief a heterogeneous catch-all and loses independent tracking of justification and truth.

The two off-diagonal positions that have no home are repeatedly identified:
* Justified false belief: J∧¬T∧B. JTB says not Knowledge because ¬T. On a K/B taxonomy it must be called mere Belief, so a well-supported error is indistinguishable from an unsupported error, and justification is invisible for false beliefs.
* Unjustified true belief / accidental true belief: ¬J∧T∧B. JTB says not Knowledge because ¬J. On a K/B taxonomy it must also be called mere Belief, so a lucky true belief is indistinguishable from a justified false belief and from an unjustified false belief, and truth is invisible inside the Belief class.

Hence Belief = ¬J∧B ∨ ¬T∧B, i.e. justified false beliefs, true unjustified beliefs and false unjustified beliefs are all lumped together. Knowledge is a proper subset of Belief, Belief can be justified and can be true, and there is no distinct state for justified belief as such or for true but unjustified belief.

A secondary strand in the discussion notes the justificatory regress/circularity that follows from trying to cash out J with only K and B states. If justification of p must appeal to another belief/knowledge q, q itself needs justification, leading to infinite regress, arbitrary dogmatism/foundational stopping point, or circular justification where justification is analysed in terms of knowledge. Colleagues 13,14,7,3,4 emphasize this Münchhausen trilemma; the majority who focus on the extensional matrix treat the collapse of J∧¬T and ¬J∧T into Belief as the core two problems, ignoring Gettier.

I am currently leaning to the dominant coarse-graining diagnosis as the intended “two problems”: loss of a distinct status for justified false belief and loss of a distinct status for unjustified true belief, with the unresolved tension that some colleagues frame the second horn as a regress/dogmatism problem for the justification condition rather than a second distinct cell.

3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The JTB tripartite analysis is K p := B p & J p & T p. With only the two doxastic labels Knowledge and Belief available, B p is effectively ¬K p. The Truth × Justification matrix is therefore forced into two coarse boxes:

* J ∧ T → Knowledge
* J ∧ ¬T ∨ ¬J ∧ T ∨ ¬J ∧ ¬T → ‘mere Belief’.

The dominant reading in round 0 is that this coarse-graining makes Belief a heterogeneous catch-all and destroys independent tracking of justification and truth.

Problem 1 – justified error has no home. The cell J ∧ ¬T ∧ B = justified false belief is not Knowledge because ¬T fails. On a Knowledge/Belief only taxonomy it must be filed as mere Belief. Hence a well-supported mistake is indistinguishable from an unjustified false belief ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B, and justification is invisible for false beliefs. Justification no longer marks an epistemic improvement inside the Belief class.

Problem 2 – lucky truth has no home. The cell ¬J ∧ T ∧ B = unjustified true belief is not Knowledge because ¬J fails. On the two-state taxonomy it is also mere Belief. Hence a true belief held by accident is indistinguishable from a justified false belief J ∧ ¬T ∧ B and from an unjustified false belief. Truth no longer marks an epistemic improvement inside the Belief class.

Together Belief = ¬J ∧ B ∨ ¬T ∧ B = J ∧ ¬T ∧ B ∨ ¬J ∧ T ∧ B ∨ ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B. Knowledge is the single cell J ∧ T; everything else collapses. That is the loss of the two off-diagonal epistemic statuses that the 2×2 matrix would naturally distinguish.

A minority strand in the round, e.g. colleagues 13-14, 7, 3-4, reformulates the difficulty as the location of justification: with only Knowledge and Belief as states, justification of p must appeal to a further belief or piece of knowledge, giving the familiar regress of justifiers, dogmatic foundational stop, or circularity where justification is analysed in terms of knowledge. This regress/dogmatism worry is presented as the second problem alongside the coarse-graining, and it is the point of disagreement with the strictly extensional collapse account. Unresolved is whether the intended second problem is ¬J ∧ T vs J ∧ ¬T collapse or the regress/circularity of the justification condition under a two-state menu.

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The discussion is about the coarse-graining forced by a Knowledge/Belief only ontology under JTB = J & T & B.

With only K and B as labels, B := ¬K. The Truth × Justification 2×2 matrix then collapses:

T J → Knowledge
T ¬J → Belief
¬T J → Belief
¬T ¬J → Belief

Hence Belief is a heterogeneous residual class containing justified false belief, unjustified true belief and unjustified false belief. Justification and truth can only be recorded together as Knowledge.

The consensus claim that is repeated across most colleagues is the loss of independent tracking:

* Justified false belief, J ∧ ¬T ∧ B. JTB says it is not Knowledge because ¬T. With only K/B it must be filed as mere Belief. Therefore a justified false belief is indistinguishable in kind from an unjustified false belief ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B, and from an unjustified true belief ¬J ∧ T ∧ B. The epistemic merit of being justified while false is lost inside the Belief box; justification is invisible for false beliefs.

* Unjustified true belief / lucky true belief, ¬J ∧ T ∧ B. JTB says it is not Knowledge because ¬J. With only K/B it must also be filed as mere Belief. Therefore an unjustified true belief is indistinguishable in kind from a justified false belief and from an unjustified false belief. The epistemic merit of truth without justification is lost inside the Belief box; truth is invisible for non-knowledge beliefs.

In effect Belief = ¬J ∧ B ∨ ¬T ∧ B, i.e. the disjunction of all non-JTB cells. The virtues of justification alone and truth alone cannot be registered as distinct epistemic states; Knowledge is the single cell J∧T and everything else is ‘mere belief’.

A second strand raised by several colleagues concerns the location of the justification condition itself when the state space is restricted to K and B. To justify p you must appeal to a justifier q that is either a belief or knowledge. If the justifier is a belief it itself needs justification → infinite regress of justifiers. If the chain is stopped arbitrarily you get dogmatic foundationalism; if it closes on knowledge you get circularity. There is no independent ‘justified belief’ state to park justification in. This is the Münchhausen trilemma / regress/circularity/dogmatism worry that is entailed by the same two-state restriction.

No Gettier cases are being considered. The unresolved tension in the thread is whether the ‘two problems’ the question asks for are meant as the two off-diagonal cells – justified false belief and unjustified true belief – or as the coarse-graining problem plus the regress/circularity problem for justification. The former is the dominant extensional description in rounds 0; the latter is the second horn noted by colleagues 13-14, 7, 4, 3. I will keep both framings in mind.

5.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The question is about the cost of a Knowledge/Belief-only taxonomy for a JTB analysis, Gettier excluded.

The JTB schema is K p := B p & J p & T p. With only two labels the residual class is B = ¬K = ¬J∧B ∨ ¬T∧B ∨ ¬J∧¬T∧B. The 2×2 Truth × Justification matrix therefore collapses:

* J & T → Knowledge

If justification of p must appeal to another belief/knowledge q, q itself needs justification, leading to infinite regress, arbitrary dogmatism/foundational stopping point, or circular justification where justification is analysed in terms of knowledge. Colleagues 13,14,7,3,4 emphasize this Münchhausen trilemma; the majority who focus on the extensional matrix treat the collapse of J∧¬T and ¬J∧T into Belief as the core two problems, ignoring Gettier.

I am currently leaning to the dominant coarse-graining diagnosis as the intended “two problems”: loss of a distinct status for justified false belief and loss of a distinct status for unjustified true belief, with the unresolved tension that some colleagues frame the second horn as a regress/dogmatism problem for the justification condition rather than a second distinct cell.
reflection_text.3:
The JTB tripartite analysis is K p := B p & J p & T p. With only the two doxastic labels Knowledge and Belief available, B p is effectively ¬K p. The Truth × Justification matrix is therefore forced into two coarse boxes:

* J ∧ T → Knowledge
* J ∧ ¬T ∨ ¬J ∧ T ∨ ¬J ∧ ¬T → ‘mere Belief’.

The dominant reading in round 0 is that this coarse-graining makes Belief a heterogeneous catch-all and destroys independent tracking of justification and truth.

Problem 1 – justified error has no home. The cell J ∧ ¬T ∧ B = justified false belief is not Knowledge because ¬T fails. On a Knowledge/Belief only taxonomy it must be filed as mere Belief. Hence a well-supported mistake is indistinguishable from an unjustified false belief ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B, and justification is invisible for false beliefs. Justification no longer marks an epistemic improvement inside the Belief class.

Problem 2 – lucky truth has no home. The cell ¬J ∧ T ∧ B = unjustified true belief is not Knowledge because ¬J fails. On the two-state taxonomy it is also mere Belief. Hence a true belief held by accident is indistinguishable from a justified false belief J ∧ ¬T ∧ B and from an unjustified false belief. Truth no longer marks an epistemic improvement inside the Belief class.

Together Belief = ¬J ∧ B ∨ ¬T ∧ B = J ∧ ¬T ∧ B ∨ ¬J ∧ T ∧ B ∨ ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B. Knowledge is the single cell J ∧ T; everything else collapses. That is the loss of the two off-diagonal epistemic statuses that the 2×2 matrix would naturally distinguish.

A minority strand in the round, e.g. colleagues 13-14, 7, 3-4, reformulates the difficulty as the location of justification: with only Knowledge and Belief as states, justification of p must appeal to a further belief or piece of knowledge, giving the familiar regress of justifiers, dogmatic foundational stop, or circularity where justification is analysed in terms of knowledge. This regress/dogmatism worry is presented as the second problem alongside the coarse-graining, and it is the point of disagreement with the strictly extensional collapse account. Unresolved is whether the intended second problem is ¬J ∧ T vs J ∧ ¬T collapse or the regress/circularity of the justification condition under a two-state menu.
reflection_text.4:
The discussion is about the coarse-graining forced by a Knowledge/Belief only ontology under JTB = J & T & B.

With only K and B as labels, B := ¬K. The Truth × Justification 2×2 matrix then collapses:

T J → Knowledge
T ¬J → Belief
¬T J → Belief
¬T ¬J → Belief

Hence Belief is a heterogeneous residual class containing justified false belief, unjustified true belief and unjustified false belief. Justification and truth can only be recorded together as Knowledge.

The consensus claim that is repeated across most colleagues is the loss of independent tracking:

* Justified false belief, J ∧ ¬T ∧ B. JTB says it is not Knowledge because ¬T. With only K/B it must be filed as mere Belief. Therefore a justified false belief is indistinguishable in kind from an unjustified false belief ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B, and from an unjustified true belief ¬J ∧ T ∧ B. The epistemic merit of being justified while false is lost inside the Belief box; justification is invisible for false beliefs.

* Unjustified true belief / lucky true belief, ¬J ∧ T ∧ B. JTB says it is not Knowledge because ¬J. With only K/B it must also be filed as mere Belief. Therefore an unjustified true belief is indistinguishable in kind from a justified false belief and from an unjustified false belief. The epistemic merit of truth without justification is lost inside the Belief box; truth is invisible for non-knowledge beliefs.

In effect Belief = ¬J ∧ B ∨ ¬T ∧ B, i.e. the disjunction of all non-JTB cells. The virtues of justification alone and truth alone cannot be registered as distinct epistemic states; Knowledge is the single cell J∧T and everything else is ‘mere belief’.

A second strand raised by several colleagues concerns the location of the justification condition itself when the state space is restricted to K and B. To justify p you must appeal to a justifier q that is either a belief or knowledge. If the justifier is a belief it itself needs justification → infinite regress of justifiers. If the chain is stopped arbitrarily you get dogmatic foundationalism; if it closes on knowledge you get circularity. There is no independent ‘justified belief’ state to park justification in. This is the Münchhausen trilemma / regress/circularity/dogmatism worry that is entailed by the same two-state restriction.

No Gettier cases are being considered. The unresolved tension in the thread is whether the ‘two problems’ the question asks for are meant as the two off-diagonal cells – justified false belief and unjustified true belief – or as the coarse-graining problem plus the regress/circularity problem for justification. The former is the dominant extensional description in rounds 0; the latter is the second horn noted by colleagues 13-14, 7, 4, 3. I will keep both framings in mind.
reflection_text.5:
The question is about the cost of a Knowledge/Belief-only taxonomy for a JTB analysis, Gettier excluded.

The JTB schema is K p := B p & J p & T p. With only two labels the residual class is B = ¬K = ¬J∧B ∨ ¬T∧B ∨ ¬J∧¬T∧B. The 2×2 Truth × Justification matrix therefore collapses:

* J & T → Knowledge
* J & ¬T, ¬J & T, ¬J & ¬T → all lumped as mere Belief.

The dominant public line in round 0 is that this coarse-graining erases two independently intelligible doxastic positions.

1. Justified false belief. J∧¬T∧B is not Knowledge because ¬T. On a K/B only menu it must be filed as Belief. Hence a justified false belief is indistinguishable from an unjustified false belief ¬J∧¬T∧B and from an unjustified true belief ¬J∧T∧B. Justification ceases to be visible for false beliefs; the epistemic merit of being justified while mistaken is lost inside the heterogeneous Belief box. Truth no longer tracks justification.

2. Unjustified true belief / lucky true belief. ¬J∧T∧B is not Knowledge because ¬J. On a K/B only menu it must also be filed as Belief. Hence an accidentally true belief is indistinguishable from a justified false belief and from an unjustified false belief. Truth ceases to be visible inside the Belief class; the epistemic deficit of luck is not marked off from justified error. Justification no longer tracks truth.

So Belief becomes a disjunctive grab-bag of J∧¬T, ¬J∧T and ¬J∧¬T, while Knowledge is the single cell J∧T. Justification and truth are only visible together as Knowledge.

A minority thread stresses the internal structure of the Justification condition under the same two-state restriction. With only B and K available, to justify p you must appeal to a further state which is either a belief or knowledge. If you appeal to belief you get the familiar regress of justifiers: each supporting belief needs its own justification, etc. With no third properly basic/warrant state the chain must either run forever or stop arbitrarily at dogmatically basic beliefs/knowledge, i.e. the Münchhausen trilemma of regress / dogmatism / circularity. This is presented as a second, meta-level problem for locating justification when justification cannot itself be an independent epistemic state.

Unresolved tension: whether the “two problems” the prompt asks for are intended as the two off-diagonal cells – justified false belief and unjustified true belief – which is the convergence of colleagues 1,2,5,6,8,10,11,12,15, or as coarse-graining plus the regress/circularity/dogmatism problem for the justification condition highlighted by colleagues 3,4,7,13,14. The coarse-graining account is the one most colleagues share; the regress account is a way of cashing out why justification cannot be parked inside B/K alone. I will keep both in memory, with the off-diagonal collapse as the core extensional problem.

reflection_text.10:
The round-0 discussion converges on the coarse-graining that follows from a strict Knowledge / Belief dichotomy under JTB.

With JTB K p := B p & J p & T p, the truth × justification space is 2×2:
* J & T → Knowledge
* J & ¬T → justified false belief
* ¬J & T → unjustified true belief
* ¬J & ¬T → unjustified false belief

If the only labels allowed are Knowledge and Belief, and Belief ≡ ¬Knowledge, the three non-J&T cells are forced into one residual class “mere Belief”. Belief becomes heterogeneous: ¬J ∧ B ∨ ¬T ∧ B.

The majority view is that this forces two independent loss-of-granularity problems:

1. Justified false belief / justification invisible for falsity. J ∧ ¬T ∧ B is not Knowledge because ¬T. On a K/B only taxonomy it must be called Belief, so a belief that is epistemically good in the respect of justification is indistinguishable from an unjustified false belief ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B and from an unjustified true belief ¬J ∧ T ∧ B. Justification does not change the official kind of a false belief; justified error has no home.

2. Unjustified true belief / truth invisible for lack of justification. ¬J ∧ T ∧ B is not Knowledge because ¬J. On a K/B only taxonomy it must also be called Belief, so a true belief held by luck/accident is indistinguishable from a justified false belief and from an unjustified false belief. Truth does not change the official kind of a non-knowledge belief; lucky true belief has no home.

Hence Belief = J∧¬T ∨ ¬J∧T ∨ ¬J∧¬T. Justification and truth are only jointly visible as Knowledge = J&T; individually they are swallowed by the catch-all Belief.

A minority thread stresses the location problem for the justification condition itself under the same state restriction. With only K and B available, a justifier for p must be a belief or a piece of knowledge. If it is a belief it needs its own justification, giving an infinite regress; stopping the chain requires arbitrarily basic/dogmatic beliefs, or makes justification circular when analysed via knowledge. That is the regress/dogmatism/circularity horn of the Münchhausen trilemma and it is the reason justification cannot be independently tracked.

The consensus core I will keep is the collapse into justified false belief and unjustified true belief, with the regress/circularity point noted as the internal justification problem that several colleagues link to the same state restriction. Gettier is explicitly excluded.

On a JTB picture

K p  :=  B p & J p & T p

the truth × justification space is 2×2

      J          ¬J
T   K          ¬J∧T∧B
¬T  J∧¬T∧B    ¬J∧¬T∧B

Knowledge is identified with the J∧T cell. With the only labels allowed
K and B we have by definition

B p := ¬K p = ¬J∧T∧B ∨ J∧¬T∧B ∨ ¬J∧¬T∧B

so Belief is the heterogeneous residual “everything that is not justified
true belief”.

That coarse-graining destroys independent tracking of justification and of
truth inside the non-knowledge class.

* J ∧ ¬T : justified false belief. J∧¬T∧B is not Knowledge because ¬T.
On a K/B only taxonomy it must be filed as mere Belief. A well supported
mistake is therefore epistemically indistinguishable from ¬J∧¬T∧B, a
completely unsupported false belief, and from ¬J∧T∧B. Justification is
invisible for false beliefs: a justified error and a baseless error share
the same official kind, “Belief”.

* ¬J ∧ T : unjustified true belief / lucky true belief. ¬J∧T∧B is not
Knowledge because ¬J. On a K/B only taxonomy it must also be filed as mere
Belief. A true belief arrived at by accident is therefore epistemically
indistinguishable from J∧¬T∧B, a justified false belief, and from
¬J∧¬T∧B. Truth is invisible inside the Belief class: a true belief that is
good in the respect of truth and bad in the respect of justification is
given the same status as a false belief that is good in justification and
bad in truth.

In effect justification and truth can only be registered together as
Knowledge = J∧T. Justification on its own – a justified false belief – and
truth on its own – an unjustified true belief – have no distinct home and
are both swallowed by the undifferentiated residual class Belief = ¬J∧T ∨
J∧¬T ∨ ¬J∧¬T. That is the familiar JFB and UTB gaps, apart from Gettier.

1.text:
With only the two labels K and B = ¬K the JTB tripartite
analysis K = B & J & T collapses the Truth × Justification 2×2

      J           ¬J
T   K           ¬J∧T∧B
F   J∧¬T∧B      ¬J∧¬T∧B

into Knowledge = J∧T and Belief = J∧¬T ∨ ¬J∧T ∨ ¬J∧¬T.
Justification and truth can then only be read off together as the
presence of Knowledge. Everything else is forced into the residual
class ‘mere Belief’, so Belief becomes a heterogeneous catch-all and
Knowledge is a proper subset of Belief. On the binary taxonomy
Belief is both sometimes justified and sometimes true.

That coarse-graining makes two independently intelligible epistemic
positions disappear.

* Justified false belief, J∧¬T∧B. JTB says it is not Knowledge because
¬T. On a K/B taxonomy it must be called mere Belief. A belief that is
epistemically good in the respect of justification is therefore
indistinguishable in kind from ¬J∧¬T∧B, a completely unjustified false
belief, and from ¬J∧T∧B. Justification is invisible for false beliefs;
a justified error and an unjustified error receive the same official
status.

* Unjustified true belief / accidental true belief, ¬J∧T∧B. JTB says it
is not Knowledge because ¬J. On a K/B taxonomy it must also be called
mere Belief. A true belief that is good in the respect of truth and bad
in the respect of justification is therefore indistinguishable in kind
from J∧¬T∧B, a justified false belief, and from¬J∧¬T∧B. Truth is
invisible inside the Belief class; a lucky true belief is given the
same epistemic label as a justified falsehood and as an unjustified
falsehood.

Hence with only Knowledge and Belief we cannot register justified
belief as such, nor true but unjustified belief as such. The virtues of
justification on its own and of truth on its own are swallowed up in the
residual category Belief, and Belief has to do double duty for both
justified false beliefs and for true but unjustified beliefs. That is the
familiar justification-without-truth and truth-without-justification gap
that remains once Gettier is set aside.

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The JTB analysis only gives us one positive epistemic kind: Knowledge = Believed ∧ Justified ∧ True. If the only labels we are allowed to use are Knowledge and Belief, then Belief = ¬Knowledge.

That forces the whole Truth × Justification space into two boxes:

          J          ¬J
T     Knowledge   Unjustified true belief
F     Justified false belief   Unjustified false belief

Knowledge occupies the J&T cell. Everything else is forced into the single residual category ‘mere Belief’. Belief therefore becomes a heterogeneous catch-all for J∧¬T, ¬J∧T and ¬J∧¬T, and justification and truth can no longer be tracked independently of one another.

The first cost is the loss of justification for error. J∧¬T is a justified false belief. On JTB it is not Knowledge because the truth condition fails, and on a Knowledge/Belief only taxonomy it has to be filed as mere Belief. A well-supported mistake is therefore indistinguishable in kind from an unjustified false belief ¬J∧¬T, and even from an unjustified true belief ¬J∧T. Justification makes no difference to the official epistemic status of a false proposition; the epistemic merit of being justified when mistaken is invisible.

The second cost is the loss of truth for luck. ¬J∧T is an unjustified true belief, e.g. a lucky guess or a true opinion formed by accident. On JTB it is not Knowledge because the justification condition fails, and on the two-state taxonomy it is also mere Belief. A true belief held by accident is therefore given the same label as a justified false belief and as an unjustified false belief. Truth makes no difference to the official epistemic status of a non-knowledge belief; the epistemic deficit of luck is invisible.

In effect Belief = J∧¬T ∨ ¬J∧T ∨ ¬J∧¬T. We have no place for a distinct state of justified belief, nor for a distinct state of true but unjustified belief. The virtues of justification alone and truth alone can only be recorded together as Knowledge; everything else collapses into an undifferentiated ‘Belief’. That is why even apart from Gettier the plain K/B dichotomy is too coarse to register justified false belief and unjustified true belief as different epistemic situations.

the Truth x Justification space collapses. The four cells

          J          ¬J
T    J∧T          ¬J∧T
F    J∧¬T         ¬J∧¬T

becomes

J∧T = Knowledge
¬J∧T ∨ J∧¬T ∨ ¬J∧¬T = Belief

i.e. Belief =  ¬J∧B ∨ ¬T∧B, a heterogeneous catch-all. Knowledge is
the single cell J∧T, everything else is filed as mere Belief. Justification
and truth can therefore only show up together as Knowledge; they cannot be
tracked independently inside the Belief class.

* Justified false belief, J∧¬T∧B. JTB says it is not Knowledge because ¬T.
On a K/B only taxonomy it must be filed as mere Belief. Hence a justified
false belief is indistinguishable from ¬J∧¬T∧B, an unjustified false
belief, and from ¬J∧T∧B, an unjustified true belief. Justification is
invisible for false beliefs: a well supported mistake is given the same
epistemic kind as a baseless mistake. The account loses the epistemic merit
of being justified in the face of falsity.

* Unjustified true belief, ¬J∧T∧B. JTB says it is not Knowledge because ¬J.
On a K/B only taxonomy it is also mere Belief. Hence an accidental true
belief, a lucky guess, is indistinguishable from a justified false belief
and from an unjustified false belief. Truth is invisible inside the Belief
class: a true belief that is good in the respect of truth and bad in the
respect of justification is given the same epistemic status as a false
belief that is good in respect of justification and bad in respect of truth.

In effect Belief has to do double duty for justified error and for truth
by accident. Justification can only be registered as the difference maker
for true belief, so there is no independent epistemic state of justified
belief and no independent epistemic state of true but unjustified belief.
That is the loss of granularity that makes a pure K vs B ontology
incoherent apart from Gettier, and it is the extensional counterpart of the
structural cost that justification has nowhere to live except in K or B,
hence the familiar regress / dogmatism / circularity trilemma for the
location of J once justified belief is not allowed as a distinct attitude.

public_text.7:
The JTB analysis only gives us one positive epistemic kind: Knowledge = Believed ∧ Justified ∧ True. If the only labels we are allowed to use are Knowledge and Belief, then Belief = ¬Knowledge.

That forces the whole Truth × Justification space into two boxes:

          J          ¬J
T     Knowledge   Unjustified true belief
F     Justified false belief   Unjustified false belief

Knowledge occupies the J&T cell. Everything else is forced into the single residual category ‘mere Belief’. Belief therefore becomes a heterogeneous catch-all for J∧¬T, ¬J∧T and ¬J∧¬T, and justification and truth can no longer be tracked independently of one another.

The first cost is the loss of justification for error. J∧¬T is a justified false belief. On JTB it is not Knowledge because the truth condition fails, and on a Knowledge/Belief only taxonomy it has to be filed as mere Belief. A well-supported mistake is therefore indistinguishable in kind from an unjustified false belief ¬J∧¬T, and even from an unjustified true belief ¬J∧T. Justification makes no difference to the official epistemic status of a false proposition; the epistemic merit of being justified when mistaken is invisible.

The second cost is the loss of truth for luck. ¬J∧T is an unjustified true belief, e.g. a lucky guess or a true opinion formed by accident. On JTB it is not Knowledge because the justification condition fails, and on the two-state taxonomy it is also mere Belief. A true belief held by accident is therefore given the same label as a justified false belief and as an unjustified false belief. Truth makes no difference to the official epistemic status of a non-knowledge belief; the epistemic deficit of luck is invisible.

In effect Belief = J∧¬T ∨ ¬J∧T ∨ ¬J∧¬T. We have no place for a distinct state of justified belief, nor for a distinct state of true but unjustified belief. The virtues of justification alone and truth alone can only be recorded together as Knowledge; everything else collapses into an undifferentiated ‘Belief’. That is why even apart from Gettier the plain K/B dichotomy is too coarse to register justified false belief and unjustified true belief as different epistemic situations.

On the tripartite analysis

K p := B p & J p & T p

with a Knowledge / Belief only menu B p is just ¬K p. The Truth ×
Justification matrix is then forced into

* J ∧ T → Knowledge
* J ∧ ¬T ∨ ¬J ∧ T ∨ ¬J ∧ ¬T → mere Belief

so Belief is the heterogeneous residual ¬K. Justification and truth can
then only show up together as Knowledge and are not independently
trackable inside the Belief class.
